subject: Can't figure out how to define parameters to trace/save

messages.author: ecbc125f147fa3ee
messages.subject: Can't figure out how to define parameters to trace/save
parts:
Hello. I'm picking up RStan again because my Jags model won't converge. 

It's fairly straightforward in Jags to set which parameters to trace and save (using the parameters.to.save command). I can't figure out how to do same in RStan.

My model is patterned after Gelman's multilevel radon model in Gelman and Hill's section 17.2 (code adapted by Peter Li here--> https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/example-models/master/ARM/Ch.17/17.2_radon_wishart.stan).

How to modify this code so as to trace/save the coefficients: a, b,  g_a_0,  g_a_1, g_b_0, b_b_1?

Many thanks in advance.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can't figure out how to define parameters to trace/save
parts:
In Stan, what's saved and not is part of the language. There are a few controls in the interfaces, but let's start with fundamentals. 

Variables declared in parameters, transformed parameters, and generated quantities are saved. Exception: variables declared in local blocks within those blocks. Variables declared within the model block, transformed data block, or any local blocks are not saved. There's no way to get them out of an interface if they've been declared there. 

To save those parameters, I'll walk through steps for just one of them. 

1. Move the declaration of g_a_0 from the model block to the transformed parameters block. 
2. Move the definition, g_a_0 <- xi_a * mu_a_raw;, from the model block to the transformed data block. 

That's it. Now g_a_0 will be in the output. There are other ways to do this, but this is probably the most straightforward. 


Daniel

Okay, Daniel. I'm stuck. Referring back to Li's code for multi-level radon with group-level predictors (once again, code is here: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/example-models/master/ARM/Ch.17/17.2_radon_wishart.stan), I'm adapting the code to investigate how land attributes are influencing algae in the Chesapeake Bay.

No problems with the group predictors (g_a_0, etc.) because they're based on parameters like xi_a and mu_a_raw, which are declared in the parameter block.

But now I want the coefficients a and b in the main linear model. I've tried expressing both in terms of parameters in the parameter block and moving things around, but my mind hasn't wrapped itself around what I need to do to ensure that I can access a and b after the MCMC run. Both a and b will be vectors of dimension J (number of counties); I tried declaring these vectors in transformed parameter block, but got errors. Then I declared them as real and looped through 1:J; also errors.

I abandoned RStan years ago and migrated to RJags, which seemed easier for me. Clearly, I'm missing a lot of RStan's logic.

Any help would be great!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can't figure out how to define parameters to trace/save
parts:
On Saturday, January 14, 2017 at 2:30:26 PM UTC-5, Pasky Pascual wrote:
Okay, Daniel. I'm stuck. Referring back to Li's code for multi-level radon with group-level predictors (once again, code is here: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/example-models/master/ARM/Ch.17/17.2_radon_wishart.stan), I'm adapting the code to investigate how land attributes are influencing algae in the Chesapeake Bay.

Part of your problem is that you chose an example that does not run. We'll fix it, but if you are having trouble getting started, you can estimate hierarchical models like this using the rstanarm or brms R packages via lme4-style syntax. In the radon case, it would be something like

radon <- rstan::read_rdump("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/example-models/master/ARM/Ch.17/17.1_radon_wishart2.data.R")
radon <- as.data.frame(radon[c("y", "x", "county")])
library(rstanarm)
posterior <- stan_lmer(y ~ x + (1 + x | county), data = radon)

Ben
